deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Front: what is the westminster system of govt?
Back:
Parliamentary system with
- a ceremonial head of state
- head of govt who leads the executive branch, with members drawn from the legislature
- legislature made of elected officials
- parliamentary opposition
- independent civil service

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back: clear distinction between executive & legislative branches, President is completely separate from the Senate and House of Commons

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- appointed by President among MPs
- President can declare vacancy if PM resigns or PM loses confidence amongst majority of MPs
- May reserve a ministry portfolio for himself

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- appointed by President in discussion with PM
- Ministers can have multiple portfolios
- Ministries may have 2 ministers covering different aspects (e.g. in 2016 MOE had Ong Ye Kung for higher edu and skills, Ng Chee Meng for schools)
- assisted by other MPs and Civil servants in their ministries
- 2nd rank: Minister of State
- 3rd rank: Parliamentary Secretaries (MPs)
- Ministers also have oversight over the various statutory boards which come under the purview of their respective ministries
- Statutory boards not staffed by civil servants hence not constrianed by civil service rules
- Stat boards are managed by Board of Directors which have greater independence and flexibility in their operations e.g. HDB, CPF

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- Power to appoint PM, declare PM office vacant (if PM resigns or if President is satisfied that PM has lost confidence of majority of MPs), withhold assent to dissolve parliament
- power to veto appointment of key appointment holders
- power to veto govt supply bills & all fiscal matters touching on SG's reserves
- gatekeeper role in decisions under Internal Security Act and Maintenance of Religious Harmony Act
- Require Council of Presidential Advisors' agreement before veto can be used
- Parliament can overrule President's decision with 2/3 majority vote
- Ceremonial role, support charitable causes
- chosen by popular election

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- constitutional office with executive functions
- AG is appointed by President and can only be removed by President on the PM's advice if he is by reason of infirmity unable to continue as AG or for misbehaviour
- Similar to UK's AGC but UK's AG is a politician, SG's is appointed by the President
- dual role of the AG
- SG's chief legal advisor - functions as the Govt's lawyer (internal affairs, civil and legislation divisions)
- Public Prosecutor - decides the course of action independently from the govt (Prosecutions division)
- Walter Woon says double role is controversial, better to split the 2 e.g. MinLaw be govt's legal advisor and AGC solely prosecutes

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1

Back:
- permission for British to set up Settlement
- formulated code of law to be administered in SG but illegal as SG had not yet been ceded to British

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- a series of laws and regulations on trade, jurisdiction and other issues
- attempted to create a modus vivendi (ideal balance) between English law & local customary traditions (on property rights, marriage and other Asian society norms)
- setting up of Registry of Land and no transfer would be recognised as valid until registered
- conduct of affairs of port of SG
- magistracy of 12 magistrates from British merchants were set up to try minor criminal and civil cases
- setting up of Resident's Court and Magistrates' Court
- native chiefs permitted to settle disputes amongst their people, subject to control of Magistracy (recognised gaps between local and English laws)

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:

- Crawfurd decided on cases based on general principles of English law while considering the character and manners of the different classes' of local inhabitants

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- Temenggong ceded control of SG to the British
- SG and Malacca were transferred to the EIC's control, fell under jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Judicature in Calcutta & subordinate to govt in Calcutta
- No legally constituted courts in SG as Crawfurd had no power to administer justice

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1
Back:
- Applies to the Straits Settlements, comprised of Penang, Malacca and SG
- established Court of Judicature for Straits Settlements in Penang. Consisted of Governor, Resident Councillors, and legally trained Recorder
- CoJ same jurisdiction as High Court and Court of Chancery in UK
- English law to be applied, and modified in application according to the local circumstances
- Criminal: administered English law with due attention given to local customs and religions
- Civil: judgment and sentences given according to "justice and right"
- unsuitable statute/case not received as part of SG law
- constitution: past laws would continue in force, subject to modifications to suit local needs
- Legislations existing in 1826 England also transferred to SG, no English statute passed after 1826 became SG law except for mercantile law (S5 of CLA, repealed in 1993)
- Presidency of Straits
Settlements formed with Robert Fullerton as Governor
- Powers to make law vested with the Supreme Government in
India, and British Parliament.
- Governor Fullerton later closed the courts
temporarily, leading to legal chaos

deck: 2 Development of SG's Legal & Constitution System 1

be in force, as long as it is applicable to Singapore’s circumstances. Judges
can modify this.

- In 1994, COA declared that they are no longer
bound by the English Privy Council, or its own past decisions.
